sourcedFrom: 930™ AND 935™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 16888, Owners Manual Rev E, typeset 2/27/18 (2018)
cleanIntro: A 935 is a 930 built for 3½" shells, and the difference that matters on a cleaning bench is the barrel: it is OVERBORED and takes Accu-Mag chokes, and slugs must never go through it. The gas system, the strip and the 200-round interval are the 930's. Unloading is the part to slow down on — shells leave the tube one at a time under spring pressure.

steps.title: Safety fully rearward, and nothing touches the trigger
steps.action: Push the safety button on the tang fully back to ON, keep the muzzle pointed somewhere harmless, and keep every finger and every tool away from the trigger until this gun is proven empty.
steps.quote: Move the safety button fully rearward to the “ON” (SAFE) position and keep the muzzle pointed in a safe direction at all times. At no time during unloading should you allow your fingers or any other object to touch the trigger.
steps.cite: 930™ AND 935™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 16888, Owners Manual Rev E, typeset 2/27/18 — UNLOADING THE FIREARM, p.12

steps.title: ⛔ Magazine tube FIRST, chamber last — not the reverse
steps.action: Turn the gun trigger-guard-up and empty the magazine tube before you touch the operating handle. Racking the action first just feeds another shell out of a full tube, and people who unload chamber-first end up cycling a loaded gun repeatedly on a bench.
steps.quote: First, remove the cartridges from the magazine tube.
steps.cite: 930™ AND 935™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 16888, Owners Manual Rev E, typeset 2/27/18 — UNLOADING THE FIREARM, p.12

steps.title: Elevator down, bolt release — one shell at a time
steps.action: Hold the elevator down with your thumb, then press and release the bolt release. One cartridge comes out of the tube under spring pressure — expect it to move with force, and keep your other hand ready to catch it. Repeat until nothing more comes out.
steps.quote: While holding the elevator down with your thumb, press and release the bolt release (Figure 4). This will release one cartridge from the magazine tube under spring pressure.
steps.cite: 930™ AND 935™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 16888, Owners Manual Rev E, typeset 2/27/18 — UNLOADING THE FIREARM, p.12

steps.title: Now the chamber — operating handle fully back, lock open
steps.action: With the tube empty, pull the operating handle fully rearward. That ejects the chambered round and locks the action open, which is the state the strip starts from anyway.
steps.quote: With the magazine tube empty, pull the operating handle fully rearward. This will eject the cartridge from the chamber of the firearm and lock the action in the “OPEN” position.
steps.cite: 930™ AND 935™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 16888, Owners Manual Rev E, typeset 2/27/18 — UNLOADING THE FIREARM, p.12

steps.title: Three places checked by eye and by finger
steps.action: Chamber, elevator and magazine tube — all three, looked at and felt. The elevator is the one people skip, and it is exactly where a shell sits when a partial unload goes wrong.
steps.quote: Visually and physically inspect the chamber, elevator, and magazine tube to be certain the firearm is completely unloaded.
steps.cite: 930™ AND 935™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 16888, Owners Manual Rev E, typeset 2/27/18 — UNLOADING THE FIREARM, p.12

steps.title: Eye protection — spatter and sprung parts
steps.action: Glasses on before the magazine cap moves. The book names both hazards and the gas system has parts that travel when released.
steps.quote: Wear eye protection during disassembly and cleaning to protect your eyes from oil spatter or spring loaded components.
steps.cite: 930™ AND 935™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 16888, Owners Manual Rev E, typeset 2/27/18 — DISASSEMBLY, p.13

steps.title: ⛔ Which front end have you got? Standard cap, or JM Pro with a spring
steps.action: Look before you turn. A standard 930/935 has a magazine cap that simply unscrews. A JM Pro Series has a magazine END cap retaining a magazine spring under considerable pressure, and it will extend to full length the moment the cap clears. Unscrewing a JM Pro cap believing it is a standard cap is how the spring and follower end up across the room.
steps.quote: CAUTION: The magazine spring is under considerable pressure and is retained by the magazine end cap. The magazine spring will extend to its full length when the magazine end cap is removed.
steps.cite: 930™ AND 935™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 16888, Owners Manual Rev E, typeset 2/27/18 — JM PRO SERIES™ BARREL REMOVAL, p.14

steps.title: Action open, then magazine cap off and forearm forward
steps.action: With the bolt locked fully rearward, unscrew the magazine cap and slide the forearm forward. The action being open is not optional — the bolt has to be back for the barrel to come out of the receiver.
steps.quote: The action must be in the open position (bolt fully rearward).
steps.cite: 930™ AND 935™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 16888, Owners Manual Rev E, typeset 2/27/18 — BARREL REMOVAL, p.13

steps.title: Barrel forward, off the receiver and magazine tube
steps.action: Draw the barrel straight forward, clear of both the receiver and the magazine tube. On a gas gun the barrel carries the gas cylinder, so it is heavier at the back than it looks.
steps.quote: Pull the barrel forward, free of the receiver and magazine tube.
steps.cite: 930™ AND 935™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 16888, Owners Manual Rev E, typeset 2/27/18 — BARREL REMOVAL, p.13

steps.title: Ride the bolt home under control
steps.action: Hold the operating handle, press the bolt release, and let the action come forward slowly. Letting it slam on an empty chamber with the barrel off achieves nothing except battering the locking surfaces.
steps.quote: While holding the operating handle, press the bolt release. Allow the action to come slowly forward.
steps.cite: 930™ AND 935™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 16888, Owners Manual Rev E, typeset 2/27/18 — BARREL REMOVAL, p.13

steps.title: Gas system off the magazine tube, in order
steps.action: Slide the gas parts off the magazine tube and lay them out in the order they came off: seal ring, gas piston assembly, spacer tube, pusher assembly, return spring, forearm retainer. ⛔ Note which way the seal ring faces — its angled surface goes outward, and it is not fitted to every model.
steps.aside: The angled surface of the seal ring* must face outward.
steps.quote: Remove the seal ring*, gas piston assembly, spacer tube, pusher assembly, gas system return spring, and forearm retainer from the magazine tube (Figure 10).
steps.cite: 930™ AND 935™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 16888, Owners Manual Rev E, typeset 2/27/18 — GAS SYSTEM REMOVAL, p.14

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Barrel, forearm, gas system, and the action if you went that far. That is as far as routine cleaning goes on this gun by Mossberg's own line.
steps.cite: 930™ AND 935™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 16888, Owners Manual Rev E, typeset 2/27/18 — ACTION REMOVAL/DISASSEMBLY, p.16

deepSteps.title: Gas rings off the piston — screwdriver, then rotate
deepSteps.action: Slide a flat screwdriver between the inner and outer gas rings, just to the left of the split in the outer ring.
deepSteps.prose: The split is the only entry point. Going in anywhere else bends the outer ring instead of opening it.
deepSteps.quote: Insert a flat head screwdriver between the inner and outer gas rings to the left of the split in the outer gas ring (Figure 11).
deepSteps.cite: 930™ AND 935™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 16888, Owners Manual Rev E, typeset 2/27/18 — GAS PISTON ASSEMBLY DISASSEMBLY, p.15

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Pry no more than 1/4", and hold it there
deepSteps.action: Lever the outer ring away from the piston by a quarter inch at most, and hold that position rather than working the screwdriver.
deepSteps.prose: A quarter inch is a real limit, not a guide. Past it the ring takes a set and never seals on the cylinder wall again — and a gas gun that will not seal is a gas gun that will not cycle.
deepSteps.quote: Use the screwdriver to pry the outer gas ring away from the gas piston no more than 1/4” and hold it in this position.
deepSteps.cite: 930™ AND 935™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 16888, Owners Manual Rev E, typeset 2/27/18 — GAS PISTON ASSEMBLY DISASSEMBLY, p.15

deepSteps.title: Rotate the piston, let the rings peel off
deepSteps.action: Keep the screwdriver still and turn the gas piston clockwise. Both rings peel off together, then push the inner ring out of the outer.
deepSteps.prose: The piston moves, the screwdriver does not. Doing it the other way round drags the screwdriver through the ring gap and gouges the piston.
deepSteps.quote: Rotate the gas piston clockwise while holding the screwdriver stationary, this will peel both gas rings off of the gas piston.
deepSteps.cite: 930™ AND 935™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 16888, Owners Manual Rev E, typeset 2/27/18 — GAS PISTON ASSEMBLY DISASSEMBLY, p.15

deepSteps.title: Trigger housing pins — 1/8" punch, either direction
deepSteps.action: Drive out the two trigger housing retaining pins with a punch no larger than 1/8", then pull the housing straight out of the receiver.
deepSteps.prose: These two are not directional, which is unusual enough that the book says so. Straight out is still the rule for the housing itself.
deepSteps.quote: Push out the two trigger housing retaining pins using a punch no larger than 1/8" diameter (Figure 12). (The pins can be pushed out from either direction).
deepSteps.cite: 930™ AND 935™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 16888, Owners Manual Rev E, typeset 2/27/18 — TRIGGER HOUSING ASSEMBLY REMOVAL, p.15

deepSteps.title: Operating handle out, then bolt and slide through the front
deepSteps.action: Pull the operating handle straight out of the bolt, then take the bolt and slide assemblies out of the receiver through the barrel hole, and separate the bolt from the slide.
deepSteps.prose: They come out the front, not the ejection port. Trying to lift them out of the top is how the slide rails get scored.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the bolt and slide assemblies from the receiver through the barrel hole.
deepSteps.cite: 930™ AND 935™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 16888, Owners Manual Rev E, typeset 2/27/18 — ACTION REMOVAL/DISASSEMBLY, p.16

deepSteps.title: Link pin — 1/8" punch — and the link off
deepSteps.action: Push the link pin out with a punch no larger than 1/8" and lift the link away.
deepSteps.prose: Last part of the deep strip. Everything past this belongs to a Product Service Center, and the book says so in its own words.
deepSteps.quote: Push the link pin out with a punch no larger than 1/8" diameter.
deepSteps.cite: 930™ AND 935™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 16888, Owners Manual Rev E, typeset 2/27/18 — ACTION REMOVAL/DISASSEMBLY, p.16

cleaning.name: GAS SYSTEM — the part that decides whether it cycles
tasks: Solvent and a brass brush on piston, rings, spacer tube and cylinder
Inside and outside of the outer ring — deposits here stop it sealing
Seal ring orientation noted before it goes anywhere: angled face outward
Light oil, then wipe back — oil in a gas system collects carbon
cleaning.quote: Normal use requires only that the mechanisms be free of excessive shooting residue.
cleaning.src: 930™ AND 935™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual, CLEANING AND LUBRICATION, p.17

cleaning.name: BARREL AND CHAMBER
tasks: Solvent through bore and chamber, patches until clean
⛔ OVERBORED Accu-Mag barrel — NEVER run slugs through it
Chokes out, threads cleaned, before the barrel is put away
Accu-Mag chokes only; they are not the 930's tubes
cleaning.quote: To ensure optimum performance, Mossberg recommends thorough cleaning of your firearm after every 200 rounds.
cleaning.src: 930™ AND 935™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual, CLEANING AND LUBRICATION, p.17

cleaning.name: STORAGE — and the cold-weather trap
tasks: Thorough clean and oil before any long storage
Never plug the barrel; never a fabric-lined case that wicks oil off metal
⛔ Below freezing, less oil not more — thickened lubricant stops the action
cleaning.quote: Over-lubrication should be avoided during below freezing conditions.
cleaning.src: 930™ AND 935™ AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual, CLEANING AND LUBRICATION, p.17

reassembly: Safety ON, and check the chamber, elevator and magazine tube one more time.
Link back on the slide, link pin flush.
Bolt onto the slide, both back into the receiver through the barrel hole.
Operating handle pushed straight into the bolt.
Trigger housing in, hammer cocked, both retaining pins flush.
Gas rings onto the piston — inner into outer first, then onto the piston.
Gas parts back onto the magazine tube in reverse order, seal ring angled face OUTWARD.
Barrel on, seated fully into the receiver, then forearm and magazine cap.
⛔ Same model, same gauge, same capacity barrel — they do not swap across models.
Function test before it goes in the cabinet.
fncheck: Safety ON, muzzle safe, and prove it empty at chamber, elevator and magazine tube. Lock the bolt back and let it run forward on the bolt release several times — it should lock closed cleanly each time. With the safety ON pull the trigger: the hammer must NOT fall. Move the safety to FIRE with your finger off: it must not fall on its own. Then pull the trigger and it should. ⛔ If the action does not lock open, or the bolt does not close fully, stop — on a gas gun that is usually the gas system reassembled wrong, most often the seal ring facing the wrong way.
